sources.entry: Splat - Native macOS Markdown editor in Rust where both the source and the live preview are editable. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/sventmueller/splat) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Splat is a native macOS Markdown editor written in Rust in which both the Markdown source and a live preview are editable, with edits in the preview translated into minimal source changes.
summary.what_it_does: Splat shows the Markdown source with syntax colours on the left and a fully editable rendered preview on the right, both writing to the same text with one undo history. Preview edits are converted into the smallest possible change to the source so untouched lines stay identical, which keeps Git diffs clean. It supports CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown, GitHub and Obsidian callouts, Obsidian wiki links and embeds, Pandoc and Typora extensions, embedded HTML, and formulas via MathJax. Mermaid, Graphviz and PlantUML diagrams render offline. Documents can be exported to PDF, a self-contained HTML file, or a Word .docx. The interface is available in 35 languages.
use_cases: write Markdown without seeing raw syntax
edit Markdown notes in a native Mac app
export a Markdown file to PDF or Word
render Mermaid or PlantUML diagrams offline
keep Markdown files clean in Git diffs
edit Obsidian-style notes with wiki links
notable: Source and preview are both editable, with preview edits written back as minimal source changes
Renders Mermaid, Graphviz and PlantUML diagrams and MathJax formulas offline
Obsidian wiki links, embeds, comments, tags and foldable callouts are supported
Untrusted image and diagram decoding runs in sandboxed helper processes
Exports to PDF, single-file HTML, and Word with real headings, lists, tables and footnotes
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple Silicon; there is no Intel build
Not on the App Store; the README says this is by design
Building from source needs Rust 1.99 and a locally created signing certificate; the README describes the build steps
Merged table cells only work across columns in HTML tables; BibTeX is the only bibliography format read
